questions.stem: A company has a short-term, unpredictable workload that cannot be interrupted. Which Amazon EC2 purchasing option fits best?

options.rationale: Spot Instances use spare capacity that AWS can reclaim, so they can be interrupted.
Compute Savings Plans lower prices in exchange for a one- or three-year commitment.
On-Demand Instances are billed for the time they run, with no commitment, and AWS does not interrupt them.
Reserved Instances give a discount in exchange for a one- or three-year term.

questions.explanation: 'Short-term and unpredictable' rules out the long-term commitments of Reserved Instances and Savings Plans, and 'cannot be interrupted' rules out Spot, which leaves On-Demand.

questions.stem: A company runs fault-tolerant batch jobs that can stop and restart at any time. Which Amazon EC2 purchasing option offers the largest discount for this workload?

options.rationale: On-Demand is the full price with no discount.
Reserved Instances discount steady usage in exchange for a commitment.
Spot Instances use spare capacity at up to 90 percent off On-Demand, but can be interrupted.
Dedicated Instances run on single-tenant hardware at a higher price.

questions.explanation: Spot is the cheapest option for flexible, interruption-tolerant workloads.

questions.stem: A company has a steady database workload that will run around the clock for the next three years. Which Amazon EC2 purchasing option reduces cost the most for it?

options.rationale: On-Demand has no discount for long-term steady use.
A database that must stay up should not run on interruptible capacity.
Dedicated Hosts add cost for single-tenant hardware.
A three-year Reserved Instance commitment gives a large discount for steady usage.

questions.explanation: Reserved Instances and Savings Plans reward predictable, long-running usage with lower prices.

questions.stem: A company wants lower compute prices in exchange for committing to a consistent amount of usage, measured in dollars per hour, that applies across EC2 instance families, AWS Fargate and AWS Lambda. Which option is this?

options.rationale: Compute Savings Plans apply to EC2 usage regardless of family, Region or OS, and to Fargate and Lambda.
Standard Reserved Instances apply to EC2 instances, not to Fargate or Lambda.
Spot is not a commitment-based option.
Dedicated Hosts are physical servers, not a usage commitment.

questions.explanation: Savings Plans are a flexible pricing model based on a one- or three-year spend commitment.

questions.stem: A company wants to bring its existing software licenses, which are priced per physical CPU socket and core, to Amazon EC2. Which option lets it see the sockets and cores of the server its instances run on?

options.rationale: Dedicated Instances run on hardware not shared with other customers, but they don't show the server's sockets and cores.
Spot Instances are discounted spare capacity that can be interrupted, with no view of the physical server.
A Dedicated Host is a whole physical server for your use, with visibility of its sockets and cores for per-socket or per-core licenses.
On-Demand Instances with default tenancy run on physical servers shared with other customers.

questions.explanation: The clue is licenses counted per socket or core: Dedicated Hosts show those details. Dedicated Instances also give single-tenant hardware but hide the physical server, so they fit isolation needs, not this kind of licensing.

questions.stem: A company needs to guarantee EC2 capacity in a specific Availability Zone for a planned event, without a one- or three-year commitment. Which option should it use?

options.rationale: Spot Instances use spare capacity that AWS can reclaim, so capacity is not guaranteed.
On-Demand Capacity Reservations reserve EC2 capacity in a specific Availability Zone for as long as you need, with no term commitment.
Savings Plans lower prices in exchange for a one- or three-year commitment but do not reserve capacity.
Convertible Reserved Instances are a billing discount that requires a one- or three-year term.

questions.explanation: The clues are guaranteed capacity in one Availability Zone and no long-term commitment. Savings Plans and Reserved Instances are discounts tied to a one- or three-year term.

questions.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with consolidated billing and the default discount sharing settings. Account A buys a Reserved Instance but runs no matching instance, while Account B runs a matching instance. What happens to the discount?

options.text: It converts into Spot capacity for Account B
options.rationale: A Reserved Instance is a billing discount; it does not turn into Spot Instances.

options.text: It applies to Account B's matching instance
options.rationale: Consolidated billing treats the organization's accounts as one for billing, so the unused discount can cover matching usage in another account.

options.text: Account B must buy its own matching Reserved Instance
options.rationale: Account B does not need its own reservation, because accounts in the organization share Reserved Instance discounts.

options.text: It goes unused because it belongs to Account A
options.rationale: That happens if the management account turns off discount sharing, which is not the default.

questions.explanation: The clue is consolidated billing: discounts apply first to the purchasing account and then to matching usage in other accounts in the organization. The management account can turn sharing off for specific accounts.

questions.stem: Which type of data transfer is generally free on AWS?

options.text: Data transferred into AWS from the internet
options.rationale: AWS does not charge for inbound data transfer from the internet.

options.text: Data transferred out of AWS to the internet
options.rationale: Data transfer from AWS to the internet is charged, at rates set by the source Region.

options.text: Data transferred between two AWS Regions
options.rationale: Data transfer across Regions is charged.

options.text: Data transferred between Availability Zones in a Region
options.rationale: Traffic that crosses an Availability Zone boundary typically incurs a charge.

questions.explanation: The clue is the direction: data coming into AWS from the internet is free, while data leaving to the internet, crossing Regions or crossing Availability Zones is generally charged.

questions.stem: A company wants to know which of its data transfers add to its AWS bill. Which transfer is typically charged?

options.text: Data uploaded from the internet into Amazon S3
options.rationale: Data transferred in from the internet is not charged.

options.text: Data sent from Amazon EC2 in one Region to another Region
options.rationale: Data transfer across Regions is charged.

options.text: Data moved between Amazon EC2 and Amazon S3 in the same Region
options.rationale: Data transfer between Amazon S3 and other AWS services in the same Region is not charged.

options.text: Data moved between two instances in the same Availability Zone
options.rationale: Data transfer within the same Availability Zone is free.

questions.explanation: The clue is crossing a Region boundary, which is billed. Data coming in from the internet, and data that stays inside one Region between S3 and EC2 or inside one Availability Zone, has no transfer charge.

questions.stem: Which TWO factors affect the cost of storing data in Amazon S3? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: The amount of data uploaded from the internet
options.rationale: Data transferred into S3 from the internet is free.

options.text: The number and type of requests made
options.rationale: S3 charges for requests such as PUT and GET, and for data retrievals in some storage classes.

options.text: The number of Availability Zones in the Region
options.rationale: How many Availability Zones a Region has is not an S3 pricing factor.

options.text: Storage class and amount of data stored
options.rationale: S3 storage is priced per GB per month, and the rate depends on the storage class.

options.text: The number of IAM users in the account
options.rationale: IAM users do not affect S3 pricing.

questions.explanation: S3 bills for how much you store in each storage class and for requests and retrievals, plus data transferred out. Uploading data from the internet is the trap: inbound transfer is free.

questions.stem: A company plans to buy Reserved Instances but expects to move to a different instance family during the term. Which type of Reserved Instance can it exchange for one in a different instance family?

options.rationale: Standard Reserved Instances give a larger discount but can't be exchanged.
Convertible Reserved Instances can be exchanged during the term for others with a different instance family, platform or tenancy.

options.text: Standard Reserved Instances with Regional scope
options.rationale: A Regional Reserved Instance can apply to different sizes within the same instance family, but not to a different family.
Spot Instances are discounted spare capacity, not a reservation that can be exchanged.

questions.explanation: The clue is changing instance family, which Convertible Reserved Instances allow through an exchange. Regional Reserved Instances flex across sizes within one family, not across families.

questions.stem: Which Amazon EC2 option runs instances on hardware dedicated to a single customer, without giving visibility into sockets and cores?

options.rationale: Dedicated Hosts add visibility into sockets and cores.
Spot Instances use spare capacity on shared hardware.
Dedicated Instances run on single-tenant hardware but without host-level visibility or control.
Capacity Reservations reserve capacity; they do not imply dedicated hardware.

questions.explanation: Choose Dedicated Hosts when licensing needs socket or core visibility; Dedicated Instances when only single tenancy is required.
